correctness.rationale: With n=2^(k+2) product_{i=1}^r p_i (distinct odd primes) multiplicativity yields exactly 2^k (P-2Q)=2^r(k+3), where P=product p_i, Q=product(p_i-1), B=P-2Q odd. Therefore k=r+nu_2(k+3), B=(k+3)/2^(k-r) must be a positive odd integer. For r<=2 B<0; for r=3 and 5 no admissible k; r=4 forces (k,B)=(4,7), prime-product bounds force p1=3,p2=5; then (p3-16)(p4-16)=233 forces p3=17,p4=249 composite, contradiction. For r=6 only (k,B)=(6,9) or (7,5); Euler-ratio monotonicity forces p1=3,p2 in {5,7,11}; modulo-3 and prefix recurrence in (7,5) force p2=5,p3>=17. Independent exact integer checks reproduced these signatures and the alleged 2023 example n=4096320, phi=1024000, tau=112, phi+tau-n/4=32. No bounded search is used as an infinite nonexistence proof.
